title: Lurkr site
description: One website Lurkr handles: sites/<id>/site.json. The folder name is the site's id (lowercase letters and digits). See README.md, "Adding a site".

color.description: The logo's colour, hex without #, e.g. "FF0069". "000000" logos are drawn in the text colour, so they show in dark mode.

domains.description: The domains links use. Each one is a checkbox the user ticks in Android's "Open by default", so keep only the ones real links use. "*.example.com" covers every subdomain but not example.com itself.

view.description: true: Lurkr can show the site itself, without the walls (the user can still route it to another app). false: Lurkr only routes it to the app the user picks.

unwrap.description: Link wrappers that only redirect (l.facebook.com/l.php?u=…): Lurkr goes straight to the link in the given query parameter.

resolve.description: Short links to follow (their redirects) before the rewrites, e.g. vm.tiktok.com/…

paths.description: Regular expressions on the link's path.

rewrite.description: What Lurkr loads instead of a link it's sent. The first rule whose path matches is used.

path.description: Regular expression on the link's path.

to.description: Load this URL instead; $1, $2 … are the path's groups.

addQuery.description: Query parameters to add (if not there yet).

why.description: What the rule is for (not used by Lurkr).

page.description: What to do on the site's pages, on top of Lurkr's shared cleanup (cookie decline, login walls, app banners, scrolling).

click.description: CSS selectors to click once per page, e.g. a "Continue on web" link.

hideText.description: Regular expressions (case-insensitive): a short text matching one hides the overlay layer around it, e.g. "keep watching".

decline.description: Extra cookie-banner button texts that decline optional cookies (exact, case-insensitive).
